text:
Running a production database on a 2 GB VPS sounds like a bad idea, but it's also a fun way to learn Postgres. This post covers how we squeezed performance out of small hardware.

We started with a `shared_buffers` setting of 512 MB, since a big cache seemed like an easy win. Then we got three OOM kills in the first month. The Linux kernel will kill Postgres when memory runs out, so the budget has to cover every connection, every worker, and every background process.

PgBouncer made the biggest difference. Pooling cut our active connections from 200 to 20. The server used less memory, latency dropped, and the VPS handled much more load than we expected.

Below are the lessons we learned, the mistakes we made, and the tuning changes that made the setup stable.
